name: Cursor
description: VS Code-based editor with an agent that can read, edit and run your whole codebase.
long_description: Cursor is a fork of VS Code built around AI. Alongside inline completion and chat it ships an agent mode that plans multi-file changes, runs terminal commands and iterates on failures. It supports MCP servers, custom rules per repository and works with several frontier models.
free_access_summary: Free Hobby plan with a limited monthly allowance of agent requests and completions.
best_for: Developers who want an agent inside their editor
Teams already comfortable with VS Code
not_ideal_for: Developers who cannot move away from JetBrains IDEs

free_access.description: Hobby plan includes a limited number of agent requests and completions each month.
restrictions: Limited monthly agent requests
Slower model access than paid plans

name: GitHub Copilot
description: Code completion, chat and an autonomous coding agent integrated across GitHub and major IDEs.
long_description: Copilot provides inline suggestions, chat, pull request summaries and an agent that can be assigned issues and open pull requests. It runs inside VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim and github.com, and is free for verified students, teachers and maintainers of popular open source projects.
free_access_summary: Free plan with a monthly cap on completions and chat requests; free for verified students, teachers and popular open source maintainers.
best_for: Students who qualify for free access
not_ideal_for: Organisations that cannot send code to a hosted service

free_access.description: Free plan with a monthly allowance of code completions and chat requests.
restrictions: Monthly completion cap
Monthly chat request cap

free_access.description: Free for verified students, teachers and maintainers of popular open source repositories.
restrictions: Requires eligibility verification

name: Windsurf
description: AI-native editor whose Cascade agent keeps track of your actions and edits across the project.
long_description: Windsurf combines autocomplete, chat and an agentic flow that follows what you are doing in the editor and applies coordinated multi-file changes. It also ships plugins for JetBrains IDEs and VS Code for teams that do not want to switch editors.
free_access_summary: Free plan with a monthly credit allowance for agent actions and premium models.
best_for: Developers who want agent flows with a familiar editor
JetBrains users who want an agent plugin

free_access.description: Free tier includes a recurring monthly credit allowance for premium model usage.
restrictions: Credits reset monthly
Premium models consume credits faster

name: Cline
tagline: Open source coding agent for VS Code
description: Autonomous VS Code agent that plans, edits files and runs commands with your approval at each step.
long_description: Cline is an open source extension that turns VS Code into an agentic environment. It works with any model you connect - Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, or a local model via Ollama - so the extension itself is free and you pay only for the inference you choose.
free_access_summary: Extension is free and open source; you supply your own model API key or run a local model.
best_for: Developers who want an agent without a subscription
Teams that must control which model sees their code
not_ideal_for: Users who do not want to manage API keys or credits

free_access.description: The extension is MIT licensed and free to install.
restrictions: You pay for model API usage separately
Local models require your own hardware

name: Continue
description: Customisable AI assistant for VS Code and JetBrains that you point at any model, including local ones.
long_description: Continue is an open source extension providing chat, autocomplete and edit modes with a configuration file that defines which models handle which task. Because it supports Ollama and other local runtimes it can run entirely offline.
free_access_summary: Apache-2.0 licensed and free to use; models are your choice, including fully local ones.
best_for: Developers who want to mix local and hosted models

free_access.description: Open source under Apache-2.0.
restrictions: You provide the model, API key or hardware

name: Aider
tagline: AI pair programming in your terminal
description: Command line agent that edits your git repository and commits each change with a sensible message.
long_description: Aider maps your repository, applies edits directly to files and creates a git commit per change so every AI edit is reviewable and revertible. It works with most major model providers and with local models.
free_access_summary: Apache-2.0 licensed CLI; you pay only for the model API you connect.
best_for: Repository-wide changes with a clean git history
not_ideal_for: Developers who prefer a graphical editor experience

free_access.description: Free and open source.
restrictions: Model API usage is billed by your provider

name: Claude Code
description: Anthropic's command line agent that works across your codebase, runs tests and opens pull requests.
long_description: Claude Code runs in the terminal or inside your IDE and can explore a repository, make coordinated edits, run test suites and drive git. Access requires either a paid Claude subscription or pay-as-you-go API billing.
free_access_summary: No free tier. Requires a paid Claude plan or API credits.
pricing_summary: Included with paid Claude subscriptions, or metered through the Anthropic API. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
not_ideal_for: Anyone looking for a free option

name: Gemini CLI
tagline: Open source AI agent in your terminal
description: Google's open source terminal agent with a notably generous free tier for individual developers.
long_description: Gemini CLI brings Gemini models into the terminal with file editing, shell execution, web grounding and MCP support. Signing in with a personal Google account grants a free daily allowance of requests, which makes it one of the most capable no-cost agents available.
free_access_summary: Free daily request allowance when you sign in with a personal Google account; the CLI itself is open source.
best_for: Developers who want a capable agent at no cost
not_ideal_for: Workloads that exceed the free daily quota without a paid key

free_access.description: Personal Google account sign-in includes a free daily request allowance.
restrictions: Daily request limit
Quota shared with other Gemini free usage

name: OpenAI Codex CLI
description: Local terminal agent from OpenAI that reads, edits and runs code in a sandboxed workspace.
long_description: Codex CLI is an Apache-2.0 licensed agent that runs on your machine and executes code in a sandbox. Access is included with paid ChatGPT plans or billed through an API key.
free_access_summary: The CLI is open source and free; model usage requires a paid ChatGPT plan or an API key.
not_ideal_for: Users without a paid model subscription or API budget

free_access.description: Install and run the agent for free with your own API key or paid ChatGPT plan.
restrictions: Model usage is billed separately

name: Zed
tagline: Fast open source editor with AI
description: Rust-built collaborative editor with an agent panel and bring-your-own-key model support.
long_description: Zed is a high performance editor written in Rust with multiplayer editing, an agent panel for multi-step edits and support for external models including local ones. The editor itself is GPL licensed and free.
free_access_summary: The editor is free and open source; hosted model usage is optional and metered.
not_ideal_for: Teams relying on the VS Code extension ecosystem

free_access.description: Editor is open source and free forever.
restrictions: Hosted model usage is billed separately

name: Tabnine
description: Code completion and chat that can run fully on-premises or air-gapped for regulated teams.
long_description: Tabnine focuses on enterprise deployment: models can be hosted in your VPC or on-premises, and it offers provenance controls over training data. A free tier covers basic completion for individuals.
free_access_summary: Free tier with basic code completion for individual developers.
pricing_summary: Paid developer and enterprise plans are available. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
not_ideal_for: Individuals wanting frontier-model quality for free

free_access.description: Free tier with basic completion.
restrictions: Limited model quality compared with paid tiers

name: Amazon Q Developer
description: Code generation, security scanning and Java upgrade agents integrated with AWS services.
long_description: Amazon Q Developer offers inline suggestions, chat, security scans and transformation agents that can upgrade Java applications between major versions. A free tier is available for individual developers.
free_access_summary: Free tier for individual developers with monthly limits on chat and agent usage.
pricing_summary: A paid Pro tier is billed per user. Check the official pricing page for current rates.

free_access.description: Free tier includes a monthly allowance of chat interactions and agent runs.
restrictions: Monthly usage limits
Some agents restricted to paid tier

name: JetBrains AI Assistant
description: Native assistant for IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm and other JetBrains IDEs.
long_description: JetBrains AI Assistant integrates with the IDE's own understanding of your project - refactoring, inspections and run configurations - and includes an agent mode called Junie. A free tier with limited quota is included with JetBrains IDEs.
free_access_summary: Free tier bundled with JetBrains IDEs, including unlimited local model usage and a limited cloud quota.
pricing_summary: Paid AI tiers add larger cloud quotas. Check the official pricing page for current rates.

free_access.description: Free tier included with JetBrains IDEs, with unlimited local model use and a capped cloud credit quota.
restrictions: Cloud quota is limited
Best experience requires a JetBrains IDE licence

name: Sourcegraph Cody
description: Assistant backed by Sourcegraph code search, built for very large repositories.
long_description: Cody uses Sourcegraph's code graph to answer questions across huge, multi-repository codebases, which is where generic context windows struggle. It offers chat, autocomplete and custom commands in VS Code and JetBrains.
free_access_summary: Free tier with monthly limits on chat and completions for individual developers.
pricing_summary: Paid Pro and Enterprise tiers are available. Check the official pricing page for current rates.

free_access.description: Free tier with a monthly cap on chat messages and completions.
restrictions: Monthly message limit

name: Replit
tagline: Cloud IDE with an app-building agent
description: Browser IDE where an agent scaffolds, runs and deploys full applications.
long_description: Replit combines a hosted development environment with an agent that can build and deploy an application from a prompt. A free Starter plan lets you try the agent and host public projects.
free_access_summary: Free Starter plan with limited agent usage and public projects.
pricing_summary: Paid plans add monthly credits and private projects. Check the official pricing page for current rates.

free_access.description: Starter plan includes limited agent usage and public hosting.
restrictions: Projects are public on the free plan
Limited agent runs

name: Bolt.new
description: Browser tool that generates, runs and deploys a full-stack JavaScript app from a description.
long_description: Bolt.new runs a complete Node.js toolchain in the browser via WebContainers, so the AI can install packages, run the dev server and fix its own errors. A daily free token allowance is available without payment details.
free_access_summary: Free daily token allowance; the original single-model version is open source.

free_access.description: Free daily token allowance that resets each day.
restrictions: Daily token limit
Large apps consume tokens quickly

name: Lovable
description: Generates React front ends with a Supabase backend from natural language, with GitHub sync.
long_description: Lovable produces a real React codebase you can sync to GitHub, connect to Supabase for auth and data, and deploy. A free plan provides a small number of daily message credits.
free_access_summary: Free plan with a small daily allowance of build messages.

free_access.description: Free plan includes a limited number of daily message credits.
restrictions: Daily credit limit
Public projects on the free plan

name: CodeRabbit
description: Reviews every pull request line by line and posts contextual comments, free for open source.
long_description: CodeRabbit reviews diffs, summarises changes, suggests fixes and learns from how your team responds to its comments. It is free for public repositories and offers a free IDE extension for pre-commit review.
free_access_summary: Free for public repositories, plus a free VS Code extension for local review.
pricing_summary: Paid per-developer plans cover private repositories. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
not_ideal_for: Repositories that cannot grant a third-party app access

free_access.description: Free for public repositories.
restrictions: Private repositories require a paid plan

name: Qodo
description: Generates meaningful tests, reviews pull requests and explains behaviour, with a free tier.
long_description: Qodo (formerly CodiumAI) focuses on correctness: Qodo Gen writes tests that reflect what the code actually does, and Qodo Merge reviews pull requests. Free tiers exist for both the IDE plugin and open source repositories.
free_access_summary: Free developer tier for the IDE plugin; PR agent is free for open source repositories.
pricing_summary: Paid team plans are billed per user. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
not_ideal_for: Teams looking for a general-purpose chat assistant

free_access.description: Free developer tier for the IDE extension.
restrictions: Usage limits on the free tier

free_access.description: The open source PR agent can be self-hosted for free.
restrictions: Self-hosting requires your own model API key

name: Diffblue Cover
description: Writes compilable, human-readable JUnit tests for Java code without using an LLM.
long_description: Diffblue Cover uses reinforcement learning rather than a language model to generate JUnit tests, so output is deterministic and always compiles. A free community edition is available as an IntelliJ IDEA plugin.
free_access_summary: Free community edition plugin for IntelliJ IDEA generates tests for individual methods.
pricing_summary: Paid editions add CI integration and whole-project test generation. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
capabilities: No code leaves your machine in the plugin
CI test maintenance in paid editions
best_for: Java teams raising coverage on legacy code

free_access.description: Community edition generates tests one method or class at a time inside IntelliJ IDEA.
restrictions: No CI integration on the free edition
IntelliJ IDEA required

name: Keploy
tagline: Tests and mocks from real traffic
description: Open source tool that records API calls and turns them into test cases with mocks.
long_description: Keploy captures real API interactions and replays them as deterministic test cases, generating the data mocks alongside. It is Apache-2.0 licensed and integrates with existing test runners and CI.
free_access_summary: Apache-2.0 licensed and free to self-host.
best_for: Teams with low API test coverage

free_access.description: Free and open source.
restrictions: You run and maintain it yourself

name: Playwright MCP
description: Microsoft's open source MCP server that lets an agent drive a real browser using accessibility trees.
long_description: Playwright MCP exposes browser navigation, clicking, typing and assertions as MCP tools, so a coding agent can write and verify end-to-end tests or reproduce a bug in a real browser. It uses the accessibility tree rather than screenshots, which keeps it fast and deterministic.
free_access_summary: Apache-2.0 licensed and free.
not_ideal_for: Teams not using an MCP-capable client

free_access.description: Free and open source.
restrictions: Requires an MCP-capable client and model access

name: Semgrep
description: Open source scanner that finds bugs and vulnerabilities using readable, code-like rules.
long_description: Semgrep matches patterns that look like the code you are searching for, which makes writing custom rules practical. The CLI and community rule registry are open source, and a free cloud tier covers small teams.
free_access_summary: Open source CLI plus a free cloud tier for small teams.
pricing_summary: Paid tiers add cross-file analysis and larger teams. Check the official pricing page for current rates.

free_access.description: The scanner and community rules are open source.
restrictions: Cloud dashboard has a team size limit on the free tier

name: Snyk
description: Finds and fixes vulnerabilities in code, dependencies, containers and infrastructure as code.
long_description: Snyk scans dependencies, first-party code, container images and IaC, and proposes fix pull requests. A free plan gives individual developers a monthly test allowance.
free_access_summary: Free plan with a monthly allowance of tests across code, open source and container scanning.
pricing_summary: Paid team and enterprise plans are available. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
not_ideal_for: Very high scan volumes on the free plan

free_access.description: Free plan with monthly test limits per product area.
restrictions: Monthly test caps
Limited to a small number of contributing developers

name: SonarQube
description: Detects bugs, code smells and security issues, with a free community build and free cloud for public repos.
long_description: SonarQube analyses code quality across dozens of languages and gates pull requests on a quality standard. The Community Build is open source and self-hostable, and SonarQube Cloud is free for public repositories.
free_access_summary: Open source Community Build for self-hosting; the cloud service is free for public repositories.
pricing_summary: Paid editions add advanced rules and larger scale. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
not_ideal_for: Very small projects wanting zero setup

free_access.description: Community Build is open source and free to self-host.
restrictions: Some rules and languages are exclusive to paid editions

name: GitGuardian
description: Scans commits for leaked API keys and credentials, free for individuals and small teams.
long_description: GitGuardian monitors repositories and commit history for hard-coded secrets and alerts before they reach production. The free plan covers individuals and small teams, and the ggshield CLI is open source.
free_access_summary: Free plan for individuals and small teams; the pre-commit CLI is open source.
not_ideal_for: Large organisations on the free tier

free_access.description: Free plan for individuals and small teams with a contributor limit.
restrictions: Contributor limit on the free plan

name: Trivy
description: Open source scanner for containers, filesystems, repositories and Kubernetes clusters.
long_description: Trivy finds vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, secrets and licence issues across container images, IaC and code. It is Apache-2.0 licensed and designed to run in CI in seconds.
free_access_summary: Fully open source with no paid tier required.
not_ideal_for: Teams wanting a managed dashboard out of the box

free_access.description: Free and open source, no account needed.

name: Mintlify
description: Docs-as-code platform with AI writing help, generated API references and an AI chat over your docs.
long_description: Mintlify turns a docs folder and an OpenAPI spec into a fast documentation site with search, an AI assistant that answers from your content, and analytics on what readers ask. A free plan covers individual projects.
free_access_summary: Free plan for a single editor with the core documentation site.
pricing_summary: Paid plans add more editors and advanced features. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
not_ideal_for: Internal wikis with heavy permissions requirements

free_access.description: Free plan with one editor seat.
restrictions: Single editor
Limited advanced features

name: DeepWiki
description: Generates a browsable wiki and architecture overview for public GitHub repositories, free.
long_description: DeepWiki indexes a repository and produces structured documentation, diagrams and a question-answering interface over the codebase. Public repositories are free and require no account.
free_access_summary: Free for public repositories, no account required.
best_for: Understanding an unfamiliar open source project
not_ideal_for: Private repositories without a paid arrangement

free_access.description: Public repositories are indexed and browsable for free.
restrictions: Private repositories are not covered by the free tier

name: Context7
tagline: Up-to-date library docs for your AI
description: MCP server that feeds current, version-specific library documentation into your coding assistant.
long_description: Context7 solves the stale-training-data problem by fetching real documentation for the exact library version you use and injecting it into the model's context. It works with any MCP client and has a free tier.
free_access_summary: Free tier with a daily request allowance; the MCP server is open source.
best_for: Stopping assistants from inventing outdated APIs
not_ideal_for: Libraries not present in the index

free_access.description: Free tier with a daily request allowance.
restrictions: Daily request limit

name: Postman
description: Design, test and document APIs, with AI help for tests, documentation and request generation.
long_description: Postman covers the API lifecycle from collection design to automated testing and mock servers, and its AI assistant can draft requests, tests and documentation. A free plan supports individuals and small teams.
free_access_summary: Free plan for individuals and small teams with monthly call limits on shared features.
pricing_summary: Paid plans add collaboration and higher limits. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
not_ideal_for: Developers who want a fully offline, local-only client

free_access.description: Free plan with limited collection runs and shared requests per month.
restrictions: Monthly limits on shared features
Small team size

name: Hoppscotch
description: Lightweight, self-hostable alternative to heavyweight API clients that runs in the browser.
long_description: Hoppscotch is an MIT-licensed API development suite supporting REST, GraphQL, WebSocket and gRPC. It can be self-hosted in a container, which keeps request history and secrets inside your own infrastructure.
free_access_summary: MIT licensed, free to use in the cloud or self-hosted.
best_for: Teams that must keep API secrets in-house

free_access.description: Free and open source, self-hostable via Docker.
restrictions: You maintain the deployment

name: Scalar
description: Turns an OpenAPI document into interactive reference docs with a built-in request client.
long_description: Scalar renders OpenAPI specifications as modern, searchable documentation with a client that lets readers call endpoints directly. The renderer is open source and can be embedded into any framework.
free_access_summary: Open source renderer; the hosted platform has a free tier.

free_access.description: The documentation renderer is open source.
restrictions: Hosted platform features have plan limits

name: Supabase
tagline: Postgres backend with an AI assistant
description: Managed PostgreSQL with auth, storage and vector search, plus an assistant that writes SQL and policies.
long_description: Supabase gives you a real PostgreSQL database with REST and realtime APIs, authentication, storage and pgvector for embeddings. Its AI assistant drafts SQL, row level security policies and schema changes. The free tier covers small projects.
free_access_summary: Free tier with two active projects, including database, auth and vector search.
pricing_summary: Paid plans start above the free tier with usage-based add-ons. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
best_for: Full-stack apps needing a real relational database

free_access.description: Free tier includes two active projects with database, auth, storage and vector search.
restrictions: Projects pause after a period of inactivity
Storage and bandwidth limits

name: Neon
description: Postgres that branches like git, with a generous free tier and an MCP server for agents.
long_description: Neon separates storage from compute so databases can branch instantly, which suits preview environments and agent workflows that need a throwaway database. The free plan supports real projects and pgvector.
free_access_summary: Free plan with multiple projects, database branching and scale-to-zero compute.
pricing_summary: Usage-based paid plans are available. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
best_for: Agent workflows that need disposable databases

free_access.description: Free plan with a fixed compute and storage allowance per month.
restrictions: Compute hours limit
Storage limit

name: Warp
description: Modern terminal with natural-language commands, agent mode and shareable workflows.
long_description: Warp reimagines the terminal with block-based output, editable command input and an agent that can translate intent into commands, explain errors and run multi-step tasks. A free tier includes a monthly AI request allowance.
free_access_summary: Free plan with a monthly allowance of AI requests; the terminal itself is free.
pricing_summary: Paid plans increase the AI request allowance. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
best_for: Developers who live in the terminal
not_ideal_for: Users who need a specific legacy terminal emulator

free_access.description: Free plan includes a monthly allowance of AI requests.
restrictions: Monthly AI request cap

name: k8sGPT
description: Open source tool that scans a cluster and explains what is broken and how to fix it.
long_description: k8sGPT encodes SRE experience as analysers, runs them against your cluster and uses a model of your choice - including local ones - to explain findings in plain language. It is a CNCF sandbox project.
free_access_summary: Apache-2.0 licensed; works with local models so it can run at zero cost.

free_access.description: Free and open source.
restrictions: You supply the model, local or hosted

name: Pulumi
tagline: Infrastructure as code in real languages
description: Define cloud infrastructure in Python, TypeScript, Go or Java, with AI help for generating stacks.
long_description: Pulumi lets you use general-purpose languages for infrastructure, which means normal testing, abstractions and IDE support. Pulumi AI generates infrastructure code from a description. Individuals get a free tier.
free_access_summary: Open source engine; the managed service has a free individual tier.
pricing_summary: Paid team plans are usage based. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
capabilities: Infrastructure as code in real languages
best_for: Teams that want to test infrastructure like application code

free_access.description: The Pulumi engine is open source; the managed backend has a free individual tier.
restrictions: Managed service limits apply above the free tier

name: Graphite
tagline: Stacked pull requests with AI review
description: Workflow for small stacked pull requests, with an AI reviewer that comments before humans do.
long_description: Graphite makes stacked branches practical by handling rebases and merge order, and Diamond reviews each pull request for bugs before a human looks at it. Free for individuals and open source projects.
free_access_summary: Free for individual developers and open source repositories.
pricing_summary: Paid team plans are billed per user. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
best_for: Teams that ship many small pull requests

free_access.description: Free for individuals and open source repositories.
restrictions: Team features require a paid plan

name: Raycast
description: macOS launcher with scripts, window management and AI commands available from any application.
long_description: Raycast replaces Spotlight with an extensible launcher: clipboard history, snippets, window management, developer extensions and AI commands you can trigger from anywhere. The core app is free and a limited free AI tier is included.
free_access_summary: The launcher is free forever; AI features have a limited free allowance.
pricing_summary: Paid Pro plan unlocks larger AI usage. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
best_for: macOS developers wanting AI one keystroke away

free_access.description: Core launcher is free forever; AI has a limited monthly allowance.
restrictions: Limited AI messages on the free tier
